index.summary: The Jackson City Council approved a claims docket of $3.74 million, including $996,580 for street resurfacing and $965,638 for traffic signal work, and confirmed three mayoral appointments to the Planning Board. The council authorized a debt-collection agreement with Municipal Intercept Company to recover unpaid fines and fees through state tax intercepts, and approved a $560,747.50 correction to the Shaw Road Bridge contract despite one no vote over contractor delays. The council also discussed street resurfacing plans, Entergy lighting concerns, and Tennis Center South management, and heard public comments on a censure petition against Councilman Stokes, flooding, and housing conditions. A proclamation declared September Service Dog Month, and the council entered closed session for litigation with no action taken.

topics.title: Public comment: censure petition against Councilman Stokes
topics.note: Norma Michael presented a petition signed by 90 citizens demanding formal censure, public reprimand, committee review, and a $500 penalty for Stokes over derogatory remarks at the Sept. 8 meeting.

topics.title: Public comment: street flooding and paving
topics.note: Diane Roby described five years of flooding on her street, saying the street is unlevel and needs paving; constituent services took her information.

topics.title: Public comment: housing and code enforcement
topics.note: Ricky Banks criticized the city's handling of dilapidated houses and unhoused residents, urging a study to help families repair homes.

topics.title: Public comment: Dale Haven Manor conditions
topics.note: Bobby Coleman described crime and poor conditions at a senior disability apartment complex and thanked officials for weekend water delivery.

topics.title: Public comment: St. Andrews Drive repaving
topics.note: Charles Johnson urged prioritizing repaving of St. Andrews Drive west of Old Canton Road, noting it has not been repaved in over 40 years.

topics.title: Public comment: street resurfacing and state match
topics.note: Virgil Payne said Hinds County has about $96,000 in leftover state allocation that could save the city 30% if used immediately for street work.

topics.title: Public comment: tax sale property issues
topics.note: Victoria Jacob Branson raised concerns about tax sale property transfers and asked the city to help homeowners avoid losing property.

topics.title: Public comment: neighborhood blight on Eminence and Newman
topics.note: Loretha Wales said two streets in Ward 3 look like a wasteland and that reported property owners have not cleaned up dumping.

topics.title: Council president apology for decorum incident
topics.note: Council President Hartley apologized for a prior meeting incident and said steps will be taken to prevent similar behavior.

topics.title: Consent agenda approved
topics.note: The consent agenda was approved 6-0 by one motion without separate discussion.

topics.title: Solid waste disposal fee ordinance introduced
topics.note: An ordinance amending solid waste facility disposal fees was introduced.

topics.title: Claims docket approved
topics.note: The council approved a claims docket of $3,741,384.90; largest claims included $996,580.16 for street resurfacing and $965,638.20 for traffic signals.

topics.title: Payroll approved
topics.note: The council approved the gross payroll and deduction claims by a 7-0 vote.

topics.title: Payment for 2525 Robinson Street
topics.note: The council approved September 2026 payment for the property at 2525 Robinson Street, a heavily used library, by a 5-0-1 vote.

topics.title: Planning Board appointment: Vanessa Gray
topics.note: The council confirmed Vanessa Gray to the Planning Board representing Ward 4.

topics.title: Planning Board appointment: Hosea Hines
topics.note: The council confirmed Hosea Hines to the Planning Board representing Ward 6.

topics.title: Planning Board appointment: James Shoulders
topics.note: The council confirmed James Shoulders to the Planning Board representing Ward 4.

topics.title: Landscaping contract with MS Yard Barber
topics.note: The council approved a contract with MS Yard Barber LLC for landscaping and ground maintenance, funded by a federal grant that requires a contractor.

topics.title: MetLife insurance renewal
topics.note: The council approved a policy renewal with MetLife for group life and AD&D insurance for 2027 by a 5-1-1 vote.

topics.title: 3P Benefits Solutions cafeteria plan
topics.note: The council approved an administrative services agreement with 3P Benefits Solutions for a Section 125 cafeteria plan by a 5-1-1 vote.

topics.title: Surplus property conveyance to Wil-Mat Investments
topics.note: The council approved conveying parcels 70-79, 110-24, and 110-25 to Wil-Mat Investments for residential development by a 6-0-1 vote.

topics.title: Entergy power line raise for traffic signal project
topics.note: The council approved payment to Entergy Mississippi to raise a power line for the Traffic Signal Group B project by a 7-0 vote after discussion of citywide lighting issues.

topics.title: Shaw Road Bridge contract correction
topics.note: The council approved amending the Hemphill Construction contract to $560,747.50 by a 6-1 vote; Stokes voted no over contractor delays.

topics.title: Municipal Intercept Company debt collection
topics.note: The council approved a resolution supporting an agreement with Municipal Intercept Company to collect unpaid debts through state tax intercepts by a 5-1-1 vote.

topics.title: Service Dog Month proclamation
topics.note: Mayor Horhn proclaimed September as Service Dog Month and presented the proclamation to Melanie Courtney and her service dog Navi.

topics.title: Office of Publication relocation discussion
topics.note: CAO Peter Davidson asked that the Office of Publication relocation be referred to committee after a building fire; the item was referred to planning committee.

topics.title: Neighborhood street resurfacing discussion
topics.note: Councilman Foote urged continuing the existing unit-cost paving contract without delay; the mayor said over 600 streets are being resurfaced and a $40 million bond package is moving forward.

topics.title: Mary Jones Community Center discussion
topics.note: Councilman Stokes raised the poor condition of the center and a family thanked police for progress in the Tayshia Fortune case; ownership and repurposing were discussed.

topics.title: Private police and armed group discussion
topics.note: Stokes raised concerns about armed groups walking through neighborhoods; Chief Brackney said open carry is legal and police coordinated with intelligence agencies.

topics.title: City workforce utilization and accountability
topics.note: Councilman Hartley asked for metrics linking spending to services; CAO Davidson said KPIs have been sent to departments and data will start monthly review in late October.

topics.title: Tennis Center South discussion
topics.note: Residents and tennis players asked for qualified management at Battlefield Park and Tennis Center South; officials said funding exists to hire a tennis pro and lighting for Battlefield is identified.

topics.title: Closed session for litigation
topics.note: The council entered closed session to discuss litigation; afterward the president said no official action was taken.
